_doc: D61 source 3: how a lemma is WRITTEN, per language. Keyed by the canonical
language code that refreshFoldContext resolves metadata.language to (tur, zho, …).
This file exists so the app can propose a citation form from the root the
morphological parse already names — 'yürü-' + this table = 'yürümek'. It is
data and not code for the same reason pos_tags.json is: a project working on
a language nobody has written a rule for should be able to add one without
touching the app.
IT MUST BE ABLE TO SAY NOTHING. A language with no entry, or an entry with no
rule for the part of speech in hand, yields NO proposal — not a guess. That is
the whole reason source 3 is separable from sources 1 and 2: a suggestion
mechanism that cannot say 'I have nothing' is the one that gets believed when
it is wrong. `zho` below is present and empty on purpose: Mandarin has no
citation morphology, and an empty object is the honest answer, not an omission.
SHAPE
<lang>.vowels   optional. Named vowel classes, for harmony. Each value is a
string of the vowels in that class.
<lang>.pos      part-of-speech tag (as pos_tags.json spells it) → rule.
rule.suffix     a fixed suffix. '' means the citation form IS the root.
rule.harmony    the name of a vowels class set to choose between, by the
LAST vowel of the root. Requires rule.alternants.
rule.alternants class name → suffix, for a harmony rule.
Nothing here changes a stored value. A proposal is text in a field until the
annotator accepts it, and an accepted one is stamped derived (B-165).
